chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Verily, God — Mighty and Majestic — revealed to Musa ibn Imran (peace be upon him): 'Whenever you stand before Me, stand in the manner of the disgraced and poor; and whenever you recite the Torah, make Me hear it in a grief-laden voice.'

key_terms.الذَّلِيلُ الْفَقِيرُ: The disgraced and poor — a symbolic description of the worshipper's spiritual state before God: utterly powerless, in complete need
key_terms.بِصَوْتٍ حَزِينٍ: With a grief-laden voice — recitation should express the soul's yearning and sorrow, not be merely melodious performance
key_terms.مَوْقِفَ: The manner/posture of standing — here signifying the internal attitude, not merely physical posture

ai.seo_question: How should one stand before God and recite scripture according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates a divine command given to the Prophet Musa (Moses), instructing him to stand before God in absolute humility and destitution, as if he were utterly helpless, and to recite the Torah with a sorrowful voice. This teaching, transmitted through a five-link chain, underscores the proper spiritual disposition for prayer and scripture recitation — one of profound awe, self-abasement, and emotional sincerity before the Divine. The Shia tradition saw in this narration a model for how to approach Quran recitation: not as a formal exercise, but as a heartfelt encounter with God.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali Bin Ma’bad, from Abdullah Bin Al Qasim, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Revealed unto Musa<sup>as</sup> Bin Imran<sup>as</sup>: “Whenever you<sup>as</sup> stand in front of Me<sup>azwj</sup>, so stand the standing of the disgraced one, the poor; and whenever you<sup>as</sup> recite the Torah, so make it to be heard in a grief-laden voice’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ali ibn Ma’bad from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Qasim from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from abu ‘Abd Allah  (a.s.) who has said the following: “

Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, sent revelation to Moses son of ‘Imran, peace be upon him, ‘Whenever you stand before me, do so like a humble and poor person, whenever you read the Torah, read it with sad voice.’”
